Source title: ISPOR/ISPE good practices for real-world data studies
Evidence-backed finding: Study questions, protocol, and analysis plans should be transparently specified and registered where appropriate.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Potential iterative drafting and inconsistencies between protocol, SAP, and clinical assumptions.
Missing quantitative evidence: Protocol drafting hours; revision rounds; rework rates.

Source title: NICE RWE Framework: Assessing Data Suitability
Evidence-backed finding: Fitness for purpose considers provenance, completeness, accuracy, coverage, representativeness, and follow-up.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Comparing data dictionaries and suitability across databases may require extensive manual review.
Missing quantitative evidence: Number of sources assessed; assessment time; rejection and delay rates.

Evidence-backed finding: Studies using routinely collected health data should describe data sources, linkages, and selection processes.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Data linkage rules and handoffs may add reconciliation and coordination work.
Missing quantitative evidence: Linkage success rate; delivery wait time; integration hours.

Source title: NICE RWE Framework: Conduct and Data Suitability
Evidence-backed finding: Substantial data curation, cleaning, exclusions and transformations may be necessary; these decisions should be documented.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Repeated transformations, code mapping, and provenance tracking may create rework.
Missing quantitative evidence: Cleaning hours; mapping error rates; effort per refresh.
Interpretation limit: Guidance explicitly recognizes curation; no time benchmark

Source title: OHDSI software tools: Data Quality Dashboard
Evidence-backed finding: DQD performs over 1,500 OMOP CDM checks by table and field against thresholds.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Failed checks may require manual triage, root-cause analysis, and remediation tracking.
Missing quantitative evidence: Failure volume; false alarms; analyst triage hours; resolution cycle time.
Interpretation limit: Shows checks exist; does not establish manual cost

Evidence-backed finding: Algorithms and codes used to select populations should be reported with validation evidence where possible.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Translating inclusion/exclusion criteria into executable temporal logic may require iteration.
Missing quantitative evidence: Build hours; cohort revision counts; logic defects.

Source title: NICE RWE Framework: Conduct of quantitative RWE studies
Evidence-backed finding: Operational variable definitions, code lists, algorithms, and validation approaches should be explained.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Code-list discovery and cross-study definitions may require expert review.
Missing quantitative evidence: Definition hours; validation rates; reuse across studies.

Evidence-backed finding: Observational studies should describe statistical methods, confounding adjustment, missing data, and uncertainty.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Repeated programming, model changes, and table production may introduce overhead.
Missing quantitative evidence: Programming hours; repeated code proportion; model rerun counts.
Interpretation limit: Reporting framework, not empirical coding-time evidence

Source title: NICE RWE Framework: Conduct of quantitative RWE studies
Evidence-backed finding: Sensitivity and bias analyses, transparent analysis choices, and quality assurance are important to study credibility.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Cross-version checks and results reconciliation may require repeated review.
Missing quantitative evidence: QA hours; detected defects; error severity; reviewer time.

Evidence-backed finding: Systematic reviews require transparent reporting of study identification, screening, extraction, synthesis, and limitations.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Screening and extraction may entail high-volume repetitive review and reconciliation.
Missing quantitative evidence: Records per review; extraction hours; field-level accuracy; adjudication workload.
Interpretation limit: Workflow standard; quantitative efficiency evidence needed separately

Source title: ISPOR-SMDM Model Transparency and Validation Good Practices
Evidence-backed finding: Model validation includes internal, cross, external and predictive validation where applicable.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Parameter, formula, code, and assumption checks can require repeated audit.
Missing quantitative evidence: Validation hours; discrepancies per model; review iteration count.

Evidence-backed finding: Health economic evaluations have structured reporting requirements for assumptions, analyses, results, and transparency.
Potential pain point (hypothesis): Reconciling manuscript, model, tables and citations may create manual consistency checks.
Missing quantitative evidence: Drafting hours; revision rounds; cross-document discrepancies.
Interpretation limit: Reporting checklist, not an estimate of time or errors
